messages:
incident-bot: Paging alert — latency surge detected for model-inference-prod in us-west-2. p95 > 2s over last 10m. Severity: high. Alert: https://alerts.redwood/5012346789

emma: I'm oncall, joining a quick bridge in 2m. starting to collect context.

maria: grabbing traces now, ping me if you need perf counters.

jay: FYI I noticed a node kernel roll earlier (03:15 UTC) to 5.15.2+ across the pool, might be relevant.

anita: confirmed deploy history: node pool was rolled 03:12–03:25 UTC, kernel v5.15.2+ (vendor build). No app change.

emma: customer impact: 3 customers with elevated tails; one has seen 429 throttles. Dashboard: https://dash/latency spike 17:23->17:40 UTC.

lucas: quick numbers — p50 flat, p95 jumped from ~450ms -> ~2100ms. suggests tail/queueing, not throughput.

maria: pulling perf counters from a few affected nodes: running `perf stat -e cycles,context-switches,cpu-migrations -p <pid> -- sleep 10`.

maria: uploading initial trace bundle to s3: s3://redwood-traces/5012346789/tracebundle.tar.gz

jay: reading the trace bundle — lots of long scheduler wake spans. example span: `sched_wakeup_wait` ~1.6s for inference worker process between wake and run.

emma: any IO or network storms? iostat and netstat show no obvious saturation.

anita: checking platform diffs: cgroup blkio/CPU CFS configs unchanged — but kernel had a scheduler tweak in changelog: "reduce migration latency" commit recent.

jay: kernel changelog snippet: "sched: adjust wake path to optimize for throughput" — could increase worst-case wake latency under certain preemption patterns.

maria: perf stat sample: cycles=1.2e9, context-switches=120000, cpu-migrations=32000, minor-faults=430k (10s window). ctx-switches higher than baseline.

lucas: elevated context-switches + long wake spans == likely preempt-induced tail latency when background housekeeping runs. matches p95 bump.

emma: mitigation proposal: isolate inference pods to dedicated CPUs (cpuset) to reduce cross-task preemption. hotfixable via DaemonSet update. alternative: revert kernel, but that's slower.

anita: I can push a cpuset pinning DaemonSet. will run on 1 canary node first.

jay: another quick toggle: sysctl tunables for scheduler, but those are risky cluster-wide. prefer cpuset canary.

maria: canary results: applied cpuset to one node at 17:42 UTC, canary p95 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~500ms within 6 minutes.

emma: great, that indicates mitigation works. start rolling to other nodes in region, 3 at a time. monitor.

anita: coordinating rollout now. will annotate k8s rollout IDs in the timeline.

lucas: hypothesis summary for RCA thread: kernel scheduler change increased worst-case wake latency under context-switch pressure. background GC/replica-sync tasks cause preemption spikes; inference threads see long wake-to-run gaps -> p95 tail. evidence: trace spans showing wake gaps, elevated context-switch counts, correlation to kernel roll. mitigation: cpuset pinning to isolate critical threads reduces contention; durable fix: vendor kernel revert or patch + lab repro.

maria: timeline so far: 03:12 UTC kernel roll -> 17:23 UTC p95 increase observed -> 17:30 UTC automated alerts -> 17:35 UTC pager -> 17:42 UTC cpuset applied to canary -> 17:48 UTC canary p95 improved -> 18:05 UTC regional rollout started -> 18:40 UTC rollout complete and metrics stabilized.

emma: customer comms going out now (P0 update): include mitigation steps, ETA for full region, and that we're working on root cause.

emma: handing the incident to jay for RCA writeup and vendor coordination. summary to include: root cause hypothesis, artifacts (tracebundle, perf stats), mitigation steps taken, and recommended next actions.

jay: ack. I'll open an RCA ticket and attach artifacts: s3://redwood-traces/5012346789/tracebundle.tar.gz and s3://redwood-traces/5012346789/perf-recordings/

maria: saved `perf record` captures to s3 path above and raw `perf report` exports too.

anita: rollout finished at 18:40 UTC, region p95 back to baseline (dash shows 420ms p95).

emma: (note) add follow-ups: 1) vendor kernel regression request, 2) lab repro with background GC + replica sync, 3) alert for context-switch spike crossing threshold, 4) postmortem with timeline + customers.

emma: closing the incident channel now. great run — 👍 to ops team.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by emma at 18:45 UTC. Severity: resolved.
